handbookNote: South Dakota Commercial Driver License Manual (base AAMVA '2005 CDL Testing System' content, Version: July 2014), published by the South Dakota Department of Public Safety (SD DPS) -- fetched via the Wayback Machine's capture of the live dps.sd.gov file (capture timestamp 20250417152533, HTTP 200, https://web.archive.org/web/20250417152533/https://dps.sd.gov/application/files/8615/0238/2848/CDL-Manual.pdf), because dps.sd.gov now permanently redirects every path -- including this exact file path, confirmed via a live 2026-08-23 fetch that returned a 302 to www.sd.gov/dps -- to a new ServiceNow-based portal, the same JS-only migration that forced the same fallback for this project's earlier sd_driver build. The direct dps.sd.gov PDF URL and the CDL manual landing page (dps.sd.gov/driver-licensing/commercial-drivers-license/cdl-manual) were both confirmed unreachable directly on 2026-08-23; the Wayback capture is a 4.72MB, 175-page PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/sd_cdl_research/sd_cdl_manual_full.txt (9,677 lines). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics are FULLY CONFIRMED, directly from South Dakota's own official manual text (Section 1, 'Knowledge and Specialized Tests' / 'What is Considered a Passing Score?'): 'You must have a score of 80% or better to pass each test.' Per-test item counts, quoted directly: General Knowledge Test (taken by all applicants) 50 multiple choice questions; Air Brakes Test 25 questions; Combination Vehicles Test 20 questions; Passenger Transport Test 20 questions; Doubles/Triples Test 20 questions; Tank Vehicle Test 20 questions; Hazardous Materials Test 30 questions; School Bus Test 20 questions -- all at an 80% passing threshold, consistent with the federal minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a). This is a direct quote from the fetched official SD.gov-hosted document, not hedged or inferred. Additional confirmed SD-specific mechanics from the same manual: tests are given once per day (a failed test requires returning the next business day); a CLP is valid up to 180 days and may be renewed once within one year for another 180 days without retaking knowledge tests; a 14-day waiting period is required between CLP issuance and CDL conversion; skills tests (pre-trip inspection, basic vehicle control, road test) must be taken in the vehicle type sought and only passed segments are banked (and only until the CLP is renewed, at which point all three must be retaken); third-party testers must schedule 2 days in advance. South Dakota's classification system: 1 (Car/Truck), 2 (Car/Truck/Motorcycle), 3 (Motorcycle), A (Combination Vehicle over 26,000 lbs), B (Heavy Straight Vehicle over 26,000 lbs), C (Commercial Vehicle under 26,000 lbs). Endorsements confirmed directly from the manual's own descriptions: T (Double/Triple Trailers), P (Passengers, 16+ design capacity including driver, applies to any class A/B/C bus), N (Tank Vehicles, permanent tanks rated 450 liters/119 gallons or portable tanks 1,000+ gallons, applies to Class A/B/C), H (Hazardous Materials, requires a TSA Security Threat Assessment with fingerprinting and an $86.50 background-check fee via universalenroll.dhs.gov, plus proof of citizenship/permanent residency), X (combined Tank + Hazardous, requires passing both specialized exams), S (School Bus, applies to any class A/B/C) -- South Dakota does not use a separate charter-bus 'C' endorsement code (its own 'C' letter denotes a vehicle class, not an endorsement). Restriction codes confirmed from the manual's own pre-/post-July-1-2015 comparison table: L (no air brakes), M (no Class A passenger vehicle), N (no Class A or B passenger vehicle), W (Seasonal CDL), V (Medical Variance), E (Automatic Transmission, new CMV-specific restriction code), K (Intrastate only), O (no tractor-trailer CMV), Z (no full air brake system / air-over-hydraulic), plus non-commercial-license restriction codes B/R/G/F/I/A/Y/C. Age requirements: 21 for interstate, 18 for intrastate. A Seasonal Farm-Services CDL (for custom harvesters, farm retail suppliers, agri-chemical businesses, livestock feeders) waives all knowledge/skills testing for qualifying 18+ applicants with a clean 2-year driving record and 1+ year of prior licensure, restricted to Class B/C vehicles within 150 miles of the business/farm served, valid for one 180-day period or two 90-day periods per year. A CDL expires on the licensee's birthday in the fifth year after issuance (with a special 21st-birthday rule); fees are $33 for the CDL plus $15 per endorsement, up to $90 per third-party skills-test attempt, and $50-$200 for reinstatement. Content-depth rationale: South Dakota uses the same AAMVA-authored '2005 CDL Testing System' base manual (Version: July 2014) used by several other CDL-track states already built in this project (e.g. Kentucky, Rhode Island), organized into the same 13 core AAMVA sections plus South Dakota-specific front matter (classification system, endorsements, restriction codes, license transfer/renewal/upgrade, seasonal CDL, fees, TSA hazmat security threat assessment procedures and disqualifying-offense lists) folded into the licensing bucket -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section, split into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through 2.23 Hazardous Materials Rules For All Drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Material (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking through 9.8 the Hazardous Materials Glossary), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, and Section 12 Basic Control Skills combined with Section 13 On-Road Driving into one bucket. Sections naturally short in this manual (Cargo: 24 questions, Tank Vehicles: 22, Doubles/Triples: 26, Basic Control/On-Road: 22) were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; Driving Safely (133 questions across two buckets), Hazardous Materials (84 across two buckets), School Bus (48), Air Brakes (45), Combination Vehicles (45), Vehicle Inspection (37), and Licensing (38) supported deeper coverage and were sized up accordingly, reflecting genuine manual depth rather than an artificial per-bucket target. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official South Dakota manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- all numeric specifications (air brake PSI thresholds such as the 150 psi safety valve setting, school bus danger-zone/mirror-timing figures, railroad-crossing stop-zone distances, hazmat background-check fees, tie-down/cargo securement minimums) were verified against the actual South Dakota text read during drafting, independently re-verified by the top-level agent against the source text and JSON structure for every one of the 14 bucket files (structural validation: 0 missing required fields, 0 duplicate-choice questions, 0 invalid correct_choice letters, 0 out-of-range weights, 0 exact-duplicate questions within or across files, across all 552 drafted questions; per-file answer-letter balance independently recomputed and confirmed within the project's 15-35%-per-letter target in every one of the 14 files, ranging 20.8%-29.2%).
